column1:
Cautiously hawkish take, corroborated by the Beige Book. The FOMC’s 25 bp liftoff, guidance for ongoing hikes, and plans to reduce the balance sheet are consistent with Beige Book reports of modest-to-moderate growth across Districts, very tight labor markets with widespread worker shortages, and broad-based price pressures. Beige Book also noted Omicron-related absenteeism and persistent supply disruptions that weighed on activity early in the period but were easing by February, aligning with the statement’s acknowledgment of elevated inflation and ongoing uncertainties. 

Credit conditions provide a partial offset: SLOOS indicates banks eased standards and saw stronger demand for C&I and CRE loans, supporting near-term business activity even as policy tightens, while households face headwinds—softer mortgage demand and expected deterioration in some consumer loan performance as rates rise. The Russia–Ukraine war adds near-term upside risks to inflation and some drag on growth.

Net: Slightly positive relative to neutral—solid activity and labor demand with supportive business credit, tempered by inflation and risk.
